analysis: The code snippet is the method `parsePropertyName`, which tokenizes a property name string and stores the tokens in a `List<String>`. It then calls `propName.toArray(new String[propName.size()])`. The list is guaranteed to contain only `String` objects because each token from `StringTokenizer` is a `String`. The array passed is a newly created `String` array of exactly the list's size, so it is non-null and has the same runtime type as the list's elements. Therefore, both declared exceptions (`ArrayStoreException` and `NullPointerException`) are avoided by the context: the array is not null, and the runtime type of the array (`String[]`) is a supertype of every element's runtime type (`String`).
remark: No exceptions are triggered because the array is non-null and of type String[], which is a supertype of all elements (String) in the list. The list contains only String objects from tokenizer, so ArrayStoreException cannot occur. The array is explicitly created and non-null, so NullPointerException cannot occur.
